thread:
maria: FYI p99 jumped ~50% on rtx-pool after the runtime push ~08:10 UTC. Allocation logs show a different kernel chosen for FlashAttention paths, plus more small KV evictions.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T08:07 -> runtime:v2.14.0 applied to rtx-pool (config: triton-kernel-selector=dynamic) :rocket:

kai: Can you paste the flamegraph or perf counters? Is it only on short sequences?

maria: Quick flamegraph: 
```
flamegraph (sampled)
- flash_attn_fwd_custom_kernel  38% (was 12% before)
- triton_attention_fallback     27% (new)
- kv_cache_lookup               15% (increased)
- other kernels                 20%
```
Seems like the runtime is falling back to a different flash-attn kernel on many requests.

ash: Logged this on a single host: `nvidia-smi` looked normal but `dmesg` had repeated soft page faults. Also saw `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT` spikes in triton logs right before kernel switch.

linh: Two hypotheses: 1) kernel-autoselect is choosing the new Triton fused kernel that is faster in long sequences but has worse latency on short bursts, 2) KV cache alignment/eviction pattern changed and causes extra memcpy overhead.

maria: Confirmed: bursting short seq traffic (seq_len < 64) had the highest p99 regressions. Batcher histogram shifted to more micro-batches after selector changed.

perf-bot: Aggregated metrics 08:00-08:30 UTC: 
- overall throughput -6%
- p50 ~ same
- p95 +12%
- p99 +48%
- small-seq QPS increased by 24% (routing change)

kai: Can we force the kernel selector back to the previous policy on a few nodes for A/B? I want to compare kernel timelines & KV hit rates.

maria: Yes, we can set env `REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=policy:v2.13-legacy` for a canary group. I'll spin up two hosts with that config.

ash: Patch to disable fused flash path (if needed): 
```
# runtime config snippet
kernels:
  flash_attn_use_fused: false
  kernel_selector: legacy
```
Will that require model reload? short restart but no model conversion.

linh: Also instrument KV cache stats (prefix hits, evictions) per-request: add metric `kv.evictions_per_req` and `kv.lookup_latency_ms` for the canary so we can correlate.

maria: Added kv metrics to canary and deployed legacy selector to 2/6 hosts. Early numbers: p99 on legacy hosts back to baseline, canary hosts still high.

kai: Good. Can we get a perf profile comparing one request path across both selectors? I want kernel durations + memcpy times.

ash: Pasted a short sample (latency components ms): 
```
selector=legacy: [kernel: 1.8, memcpy: 0.4, kv_lookup: 0.5, total: 3.0]
selector=dynamic: [kernel: 2.9, memcpy: 1.1, kv_lookup: 1.5, total: 5.5]
```
memcpy & kv_lookup are the big delta.

linh: That indicates the kernel choice increases cache misses and triggers larger device-host churn. Possibly different shared memory / alignment assumptions in the fused kernel.

maria: Short-term mitigation: pin selector to legacy for small-seq traffic and add a routing rule to prefer legacy for seq_len < 128. Also open bug with Triton/FlashAttention team.

kai: Long-term: add selector cost model that accounts for memcpy and KV penalties (not just kernel speed). TODO: model bench across sequence distributions and include in selector scoring.

perf-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-042: p99 regression due to kernel selector change. Tags: triton, flash-attn, kv-cache, runtime.

maria: I'm going to roll forward this routing change and keep canary monitoring for 2 hours. Ping me if you see any anomalies. :white_check_mark:

ash: If rollback needed we have `runtime:v2.13.8` pinned as last-known-good.

kai: Great work. Follow-up actions: 1) perf microbench across seq bins, 2) KV instrumentation retention for 72h, 3) selector scoring change. I'll schedule sync tomorrow.

linh: Filing a PR with additional KV metrics and a minimal repro that hits the fused kernel path.

maria: Thanks everyone — keeping the thread updated as canary data rolls in.
